questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before going, I had heard many positive things about going on exchange to Milan. For me, it was a combination of the academic opportunities, the chance to meet new people, as well as the food and the culture that made me want to go there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my Erasmus exchange in Milan, where I met many great people from all over Europe and the world. During my stay, I had the opportunity to experience beautiful nature and cities, as well as taste a variety of delicious food and wines.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, I think the preparation process was satisfactory. I received many emails from the university in Milan informing me about the next steps, and I was also contacted regarding accommodation. However, efficiency is not a word Italians like, and it is necessary to be patient when waiting for replies, whether from the university or in relation to accommodation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Italian Erasmus coordinator, Massimo, was very helpful. He could easily be contacted by email and usually had a solution or an answer to any questions. He also has a office you can go to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: When i applied for the University, i could check a box off, asking whether or not i would like the University to find some housing for me. So it was really easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I lived at Campus Martinitt, which was very affordable. I paid approximately €300 per month. However, the rooms are shared, meaning that you live with another person. In my case, this worked well, as I was fortunate to have a nice flatmate. Unfortunately, some of my friends were less lucky and experienced roommates who were rather disrespectful.

Although the dormitory is quite large, with approximately 300 – 400 residents, there was only one shared kitchen for everyone. As a result, it was often very unhygienic, especially in the evenings. The rooms are quite old and not particularly appealing, but each room has a private bathroom, which was cleaned regularly by the staff. Bed sheets were also changed every two weeks, which was a positive aspect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before arrival, you receive links by email where you can find information about the available courses. Course registration takes place after arrival, and it is therefore not necessary to register for courses in advance. This allows you to change courses if they do not meet your expectations or fit your schedule. Once you have decided which courses you wish to take, you simply register for them through the university’s online platform.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot of help, i just figured it out my self

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I changed three out of my four initial courses, as they did not fit together at all. However, everything worked out well in the end. Patientce is the key word.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to try out several different courses before registering for them. Additionally, I would recommend choosing courses from the same degree programme, as all the first exam sessions are typically scheduled in January. I would also strongly recommend asking the professors in advance when they plan to hold the exams. I did not fully realize this until it was too late, which resulted in having five exams within a ten day period. This was a very stressful experience.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took master’s level courses, as there were no English taught courses available at the bachelor level. However, I found that the academic level of the master’s courses was generally comparable to, or in some cases slightly lower than, the level of bachelor’s courses in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Milan, teaching mainly consisted of two to three hour lectures where students primarily listened to the professor. There were no exercises, laboratory work, or group assignments. I found this teaching style monotone, and at times the quality of the teaching was limited, partly because some professors were not very proficient in English.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Methods in Bioinformatics 
- Molecular and Cellular Microbiology
- Genetics, Cellular and Molecular Biology
- Biotechnological Products and Processes

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course in Bioinformatics, as the exam consisted of a project that could be completed either individually or in groups.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy a new phone, since my old one got stolen. I also spend quite a lot of money on traveling around.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were generally cheaper than in Denmark, and I also found that eating at restaurants was slightly more affordable. As a result, we ate out quite frequently. Beer prices were more or less the same as in Denmark, whereas wine was very cheap. Public transportation was also very affordable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN (Erasmus student network), organize a lot of different activites, sports and parties. They also plan trips to rome or even germany.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend travelling around with friends during the exchange. We visited Rome, which was a great experience, and we also spent a few days in Morocco, which was very exciting. Additionally, Milan itself offers many opportunities for social activities, whether it is going to a bar, a restaurant, or a club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- Go to some of the cities near milan
- Grab a beer with some friends
- Go on a hike

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy. I quickly met some new people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really. Most of the people that i spoke with and befriended was also exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I experienced a relatively high level of bureaucracy, and administrative processes were sometimes inefficient, which required a lot of patience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italy has excellent food and wine, as well as many impressive monuments with a long history. I also loved that coffee is so cheap there.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Meet new people from other countries and cultures. Don’t only socialize with other Danes, otherwise you won’t learn much.
- Be very patient.
- Save some money in advance. I ended up spending much more than I initially expected.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit stressfull going on exchange, but everything will work out, since there is a solution for almost everything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: When i passed all my exams. I had five exams in ten days. I was sure that i could not do it. But it all, worked out in the end. It always does.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding courses that fit into my schedule was challenging. I also did not particularly enjoy the teaching style in Italy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
